item.title: Google DeepMind Prioritizes Lifelong Learning Over Degrees in Hiring
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: One of Google DeepMind's top execs says lifelong learners will have an edge in the AI workplace
Lila Ibrahim, Google DeepMind's chief AI readiness officer, emphasized that candidates with a lifelong learning mindset are prioritized over traditional degrees. At a media event, she stated that multiple credentials demonstrate a commitment to learning, which is crucial in an AI-driven workplace. She noted that modern resumes often highlight non-formal learning experiences, revealing curiosity and adaptability. Ibrahim argued that asking good questions—often untaught in schools—is vital as AI makes information easily accessible. DeepMind seeks individuals with curiosity, courage to tackle new challenges, and collaboration skills. Ibrahim highlighted the need for interdisciplinary teams, combining STEM and humanities like philosophy and ethics, to drive innovation. Google DeepMind founder Demis Hassabis echoed this, stressing the importance of humanities alongside technical skills. A study found that while 75% of companies use AI, only 18% have upskilled most employees. Ibrahim noted increased diversity in UK talent for philosophy and political science compared to Silicon Valley. AI is reshaping jobs, requiring workers to develop both technical and human skills.

item.title: Del Mar council approves speed limit changes
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Del Mar council approves second reading of updated speed limits
Del Mar City Council voted Oct. 20 to approve a second reading of updated speed limits at eight locations, effective in 30 days. Four segments on Camino Del Mar will see speed limits reduced from 40 mph to 30 mph and from 35 mph to 30 mph. Three segments along Jimmy Durante Boulevard will lower from 45 mph to 40 mph, 45 mph to 30 mph, and 35 mph to 30 mph. A segment on Via de la Valle will decrease from 40 mph to 35 mph. The changes follow a Traffic and Parking Advisory Committee recommendation based on speed surveys. The 85th percentile speed, determined by regular surveys, guides the adjustments. California law allows speed limits to be set at the nearest 5 mph increment of the 85th percentile or reduced by 5 mph through engineering judgment, especially in areas with injury or fatality patterns.

item.title: SANDAG Awards $4.5M for Microtransit Pilot Projects in San Diego
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: SANDAG Board Approves $4.5M for Seven Microtransit Pilot Projects
SANDAG awarded $4.5 million to seven microtransit pilot projects across San Diego. The Flexible Fleets Pilot Grant Program funds on-demand shared transportation like electric shuttles, minivans, and small buses. The initiative aims to expand travel options, improve air quality, and provide first- and last-mile connections in underserved areas. SANDAG Chair Lesa Heebner emphasized the importance of partnerships with non-profits, local governments, and service providers to create a regional model. Recipients include North County Transit - San Diego Railroad ($810,000), UC San Diego ($246,650), Chula Vista ($375,000), and Solana Beach ($208,966). Services will focus on campus mobility, reduced commuting times, and access to medical appointments. Some projects are set to launch next year, building on prior pilots like the Beach Bug and gO'side Shuttle.

item.title: AI Agents Help Manage Daily Tasks, Raising Privacy Concerns
item.description:
Source: Vox Original headline: When AI agents run your life
AI agents like Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots are helping users manage daily tasks, offering convenience but raising privacy concerns. Sari Azout, a tech worker and mother of three, found relief using an AI agent to handle back-to-school logistics, feeling 'calm and present' for the first time. Reece Rogers, a Wired reporter, describes agents as proactive digital assistants that scan emails and calendars for help. Muse, which integrates with Facebook Marketplace, and Dots, a paid tool, are among the popular options. Users report benefits like finding couches within budget or canceling subscriptions, but privacy risks loom. Muse requests access to emails, bank accounts, and passport details, with interactions automatically used to train Meta's AI. Rogers warns of potential mishaps, like an AI posting bank balances to Slack. Companies are countering distrust with cute mascots, blending cuteness with functionality. Despite skepticism, Rogers predicts AI agents will become mainstream, echoing the rise of ChatGPT, as they promise to free up time for leisure. However, users must balance convenience with data sharing risks.

item.title: Uganda mandates 21-day quarantine for citizens returning from DR Congo
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: Uganda imposes 21-day quarantine on citizens returning from DR Congo
Uganda requires citizens returning from DR Congo to undergo 21 days of quarantine at their own cost, as the country intensifies measures to prevent Ebola spread. Over 4,800 deaths have occurred in DR Congo since May, with the virus spreading to neighboring nations. Two Ebola cases in Kenya and Nigeria, linked to travel through Uganda, prompted the restrictions. The health ministry confirmed 60 contacts of the Kenyan patient were discharged and barred transit through Uganda. Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi stated only essential travelers from DR Congo would be allowed in, subject to strict public health protocols. Uganda claims no domestic cases but faces scrutiny after the Kenyan patient died in Nairobi and Nigeria confirmed eight cases. Officials are investigating the Nigerian patient’s travel history, with CCTV showing no interaction between the two infected individuals. The Bundibugyo Ebola strain, with no vaccine or treatment available, continues to spread in DR Congo, prompting vigilance along the shared border.

item.title: Del Mar Appoints Steven McDowell to Undergrounding Committee
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Del Mar council appoints Steven McDowell to undergrounding committee
Del Mar City Council appointed Steven McDowell to the Undergrounding Program Advisory Committee following a vote on October 20. The seven-member committee oversees the city’s utility undergrounding project, now in its initial phases. McDowell, a Del Mar resident also serving on the Finance Committee, was the sole applicant to fill a citizen interest form after committee member John Imperato resigned in September. In his form, McDowell emphasized his financial modeling expertise, knowledge of street impact assessments, and experience in finance and program management. He also highlighted his desire to learn about project logistics and contribute to discussions on financing, timelines, and neighborhood communication. McDowell previously served on the Traffic and Parking Advisory Committee from 2004 to 2012.

item.title: UK urges families to stockpile three days' essentials amid rising threats
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Families should stockpile 3 days' worth of essentials in today's world of disaster and war, the UK warns
UK officials urge families to stockpile three days' worth of essentials amid rising risks of disasters, conflicts, and cyber threats. Prime Minister Andy Burnham's office launched the 'Be Ready' campaign, advising households to prepare non-perishable food, water, hygiene products, warm clothing, lighting, cash, and medical supplies. The initiative aims to ensure survival during emergencies when supply chains may fail. Burnham emphasized taking 'sensible measures' without panic, while defense minister Wes Streeting warned of increased threats from both state actors and criminals. The campaign encourages gradual stockpiling and regular checks for expired items. Recent events included a global website outage due to a security flaw in widely used software and power outages from storms in northern Europe. Streeting also highlighted the growing military threat from adversaries, stating the UK has 1,000 days to enhance national resilience against potential war scenarios.

item.title: Researchers Explore Link Between Disgust and Political Beliefs
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated
Researchers explore how disgust relates to political beliefs, finding links between disgust sensitivity and socially conservative views. A review of 24 studies found people more easily disgusted tended to hold conservative attitudes. Psychologist Yoel Inbar notes disgust evolved to avoid pathogens, linking it to traditional social norms. The Three-Domain Disgust Scale distinguishes pathogen, sexual, and moral disgust. A 2020 study showed conservatives reported greater disgust at sexual behaviors and drug use, while liberals found animal abuse and environmental pollution revolting. Interoceptive sensibility research by Tsakiris and von Mohr found conservatives linked to sexual disgust, but moral disgust ties to conservatism only among low bodily awareness individuals. Inbar questions if all disgust types are useful for political analysis, preferring pathogen disgust. He cautions the relationship is small and complex. Tsakiris argues political messages may exploit disgust by labeling emotions, urging critical examination of feelings. The study cannot determine if disgust shapes beliefs or vice versa, with Bakker noting political beliefs influence self-perception. Inbar emphasizes disgust is one of many factors in politics.

item.title: USS Spruance Breaks Record for Longest Destroyer Deployment
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: San Diego’s USS Spruance breaks record for longest deployment by a destroyer
The USS Spruance, based in San Diego, has set a new record for the longest deployment by a destroyer since World War II, reaching 339 days. The ship surpassed the previous record of 333 days held by the USS McFaul. The Spruance’s mission was extended beyond its initial seven-month plan when the U.S. entered conflict with Iran in February. The 510-foot destroyer, with a crew of 330 sailors, played a key role in missile strikes against Iran, enforced a naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz, and protected the USS Abraham Lincoln Carrier Strike Group from drone and missile attacks. The Lincoln returned to San Diego in October, but the Spruance remained in the Indo-Pacific due to the Navy’s shipbuilding and repair challenges. The ship is named after Adm. Ray Spruance, who led the U.S. to victory in the Battle of Midway in 1942. Historians note his actions there were a turning point in World War II. The Spruance is expected to return to San Diego in November, though an exact date has not been announced.

item.title: AI Enhances Hurricane Forecast Accuracy
item.description:
Source: NPR Topics: News Original headline: How AI is transforming hurricane forecasts
AI models are outperforming traditional hurricane forecasting systems, with Google DeepMind's model accurately predicting Hurricane Isaias's path. Meteorologists note the AI's reliance on historical data patterns rather than physics-based equations. The National Hurricane Center now uses a blend of AI and traditional models for forecasts, emphasizing human interpretation of results. While AI updates improve rapidly, traditional models still offer critical insights. Experts highlight the AI's speed of advancement, with skill gains achieved in months rather than years. However, AI models like DeepMind still face challenges in intensity predictions, requiring ongoing refinement. Human forecasters remain essential for translating model outputs into actionable warnings for the public.

item.title: Big Law Firms Send Most Lawyers to Tech Giants
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: The Big Law firms sending the most lawyers into Big Tech's arms
Big Law firms are losing lawyers to tech companies. New data from Pirical, a legal people-analytics firm, shows Morrison Foerster and Wilson Sonsini tied for the most alumni in legal roles at major tech firms, with 40 each. Latham & Watkins had 33, while Kirkland & Ellis ranked 11th with 21. Cooley, despite being 29th in revenue, had 29 alumni at tech firms. Davis Wright Tremaine and Fenwick also had notable numbers. The shift is driven by better pay, fewer clients, and involvement in AI legal challenges. Google employs the most alumni from top law firms, though its size may explain the count. Recruiters note these roles offer 'highly desirable' opportunities, with tech firms tackling complex legal issues. Pirical's analysis may miss some lawyers due to outdated profiles or non-standard job titles.

item.title: Nvidia Names New Sales and Marketing Leaders Amid Leadership Shift
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Nvidia's sales and marketing leadership is seeing a changing of the guard — and new faces are gaining influence
Nvidia is reshaping its sales and marketing leadership as the AI boom drives changes. The company is replacing veteran executives with outsiders, including Google Cloud's Alison Wagonfeld as chief marketing officer and Microsoft's Nick Parker as sales chief. CEO Jensen Huang's daughter, Madison Huang, has gained influence beyond her formal role, overseeing physical AI marketing and strategic decisions. Retirees this year include Jay Puri, Laura Fay, Shanker Trivedi, and Kevin Connors. Trivedi, who retired after 17 years, emphasized mentorship for younger talent, noting Nvidia's 'deep bench' of experienced leaders. Scott Baker, a 26-year veteran, described the company's rapid evolution. Madison, who previously worked at LVMH, now holds a senior director role and collaborates closely with Huang. Huang regularly reshapes Nvidia's structure to adapt to market demands, splitting Trivedi's responsibilities to streamline operations. The company's revenue growth during the AI boom has accelerated these changes.

item.title: State Urges Del Mar to Finalize Bluff Zoning by Nov. 16
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: State warns Del Mar to complete fairgrounds backup zoning
Del Mar has until Nov. 16 to finalize north and south bluff upzones or risk losing housing element compliance. The city’s housing plan, which aimed to meet 113 lower-income units via a fairgrounds project, is now in jeopardy after the fairgrounds board ended discussions in August. HCD’s letter states the city failed to implement Program 1E, citing a 54-unit shortfall in its housing element. The city’s response claimed alternate sites could meet RHNA requirements, but HCD noted these sites were not analyzed. North bluff owner Carol Lazier’s court petition argues her 259-unit proposal should qualify for by-right development. Mayor Tracy Martinez pledged to address HCD’s concerns. HCD will review the city’s response before deciding on enforcement actions.

item.title: San Diego Jail Commissary System Outage Continues
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Outage continues for San Diego County’s jail commissary
San Diego County jails' commissary system remains offline after four days of technical issues. The outage began Thursday evening, prompting officials to shut down the system to prevent further complications. Commissary operations are not expected to resume until at least Wednesday. Family members of incarcerated individuals cannot purchase items or add funds, while inmates are unable to order supplies. Public access to the system is also blocked. Sheriff’s Office Reentry Services Manager Michelle Aguinaldo acknowledged the disruption’s impact, stating, 'We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this disruption may cause.' Officials noted they are collaborating with vendors to resolve the issue and restore full functionality.

item.title: Solana Beach Civic & Historical Society Hosts Annual Holiday Boutique
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Solana Beach Civic & Historical Society to hold Annual Holiday Boutique
The Solana Beach Civic & Historical Society hosts its 73rd Annual Holiday Boutique on Saturday, Nov. 14, at the La Colonia Community Center. The event runs from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m., featuring hand-made gifts, home-baked goods, and unique crafts. Items include holiday gifts, children’s and pet toys, home décor, planters, paper art, jewelry, and quilts. Baked goods range from cookies to fudge. A quilt drawing offers a Bookshelf Themed Quilt. Free coffee is available on the patio, where the SeaWeeders Garden Club sells Christmas cactus and takes poinsettia orders. Proceeds fund student scholarships and community programs.

item.title: SBCC Distributes Holiday Gift Baskets to Solitary Seniors
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Help warm a senior’s heart with a Holiday Gift Basket
Solana Beach Community Connections (SBCC) is preparing Holiday Gift Baskets for senior residents living alone. The initiative targets 'Solo-Agers' who may have lost spouses or live isolated. SBCC aims to identify eligible seniors and collect donation items for baskets. Donations can be dropped off at Solana Beach City Hall from Nov. 2 to Dec. 10, with items including calendars, puzzles, hot chocolate, mugs, nightlights, and socks. The city partners with SBCC, providing a donation location. Contributions can also be mailed as checks payable to SBCC. The organization, a volunteer-driven 501(c)(3) nonprofit, invites community members to help assemble or fund baskets. Contact info@solanabeachcc.org for details.

item.title: Encinitas Hosts 13th Annual Día de los Muertos Festival
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: 13th Annual Encinitas Día de los Muertos Celebration
Encinitas Friends of the Arts, MiraCosta College, Mano a Mano Foundation, and the City of Encinitas hosted the 13th Annual Día de los Muertos Celebration on October 25 at MiraCosta College San Elijo Campus. The event honored Mexican and Latino traditions through a community Ofrenda blessing by Danza Azteca Mission San Luis Rey, remarks from leaders, live performances, workshops, art displays, a lowrider car show, artisan vendors, authentic food, and opportunity drawings. The festival brought together families and communities to commemorate loved ones, featuring cultural activities and local businesses. Artwork was available for purchase, and the event emphasized cultural heritage through interactive experiences and public engagement.

item.title: Caltrans, SANDAG to Resume Rail Work in Batiquitos Lagoon This Weekend
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego
Caltrans and San Diego Association of Governments will resume rail work in Batiquitos Lagoon this weekend. The project, delayed by weather, involves rail destressing and trackwork installation south of La Costa Avenue overcrossing. The double-track initiative aims to enhance the LOSSAN rail corridor's capacity by adding a second track from Avenida Encinas to La Costa Avenue, allowing uninterrupted train travel. The existing 80-year-old wooden trestle bridge will be replaced with a modern steel-and-concrete structure, widening lagoon channels to improve tidal flow for wildlife. Construction noise, equipment sounds, and additional lighting will be present. Work begins 10 p.m. Saturday and ends 4 a.m. Sunday.

item.title: Tree Trimmer Rescued From San Diego Apartment Roof
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: Tree trimmer rescued from apartment building roof in Colina Del Sol
A 72-year-old man was rescued from the roof of a three-story apartment building in San Diego's Colina Del Sol neighborhood Sunday afternoon. Firefighters used a pulley system and a basket to lower him to the ground within about 50 minutes. The incident occurred at 4253 49th St., where the man had climbed onto the roof to trim tree branches but was unable to descend. Emergency responders included two fire engines, a fire truck, an urban search and rescue unit, an ambulance, a battalion chief, and a shift commander. The man was evaluated and released by medics on scene. Authorities urged residents to prepare for potential El Nino storms but emphasized safety precautions.

item.title: Six Flags Adds Seat Belts to Some Rides After Georgia Death
item.description:
Source: Washington Post Original headline: Six Flags to add seat belts to some roller coasters after death in Georgia
Six Flags announced plans to add seat belts to some roller coasters following the death of Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, 42, who fell from the Goliath ride at its Georgia park on October 12. The company’s CEO, John Reilly, stated the move includes seat belts on Goli'th and similar coasters. Goliath remains closed for safety reviews, with eight rides at other parks temporarily shut down. Investigators found Ibn Kariem was ejected from the ride, struck other patrons, and fell beneath the attraction. The 200-foot-tall Goliath, with a 70 mph top speed, used lap bars for restraint. Georgia’s Insurance and Safety Fire Commissioner’s office is conducting an in-depth review of the ride’s safety compliance, noting no violations were reported during its last March inspection. The incident follows Six Flags Magic Mountain’s decision to permanently close its X2 coaster amid lawsuits over alleged brain injuries.

item.title: CEO Near Launch of Psilocybin Pill After Years of Trials
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: After a long, strange trip, this CEO is close to taking a psilocybin pill to market
Kabir Nath, former pharmaceutical executive, joined Compass Pathways in 2022 to lead development of a psilocybin pill for treatment-resistant depression. His decision followed his father's suicide and a belief in the drug's potential. Compass, now with 150 new hires and expanded operations, aims for FDA approval by next year. Recent trials showed nearly half of participants experienced at least a 50% reduction in depressive symptoms within six weeks. The company faces uncertainty, as FDA approval is not guaranteed, and a rejection could lead to bankruptcy. Nath emphasized the need for the drug, noting 4 million U.S. patients struggle with ineffective antidepressants. Compass is preparing for potential market entry, including training sales teams and engaging healthcare providers. The FDA's rigorous evaluation process applies to all psychedelic drug applications, with Compass facing a decision by mid-2024. Other companies, like AtaiBeckley, also seek approval for similar treatments, highlighting the growing interest in psychedelics as medical therapies.

item.title: Solana Beach holds Día de los Muertos event for 40th city anniversary
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Annual Día de los Muertos event held in Solana Beach
Solana Beach’s annual Día de los Muertos event took place Oct. 18 at La Colonia Park. Organized by the City of Solana Beach and the La Colonia Community Foundation, the event celebrated the 40th anniversary of the city’s founding. Cultural activities included Mexican American food, entertainment, and contests for costumes and face masks. Over 40 altars were displayed to honor deceased family and friends. The Lenahan famly (Jon Clark) was among those involved. The event also highlighted the ancestral legacy of La Colonia de Eden Gardens, blending tradition with community celebration. Attendees participated in kid-friendly activities while paying tribute to loved ones through the iconic altars central to Día de los Muertos traditions.

item.title: PROFILE: Kim Weinstein Named Del Mar Community Connections Volunteer of the Month
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Del Mar Community Connections names Kim Weinstein October Volunteer of the Month
Kim Weinstein, a volunteer chair yoga instructor and program leader, was named Del Mar Community Connections Volunteer of the Month. Carol German, DMCC’s Program Committee chair, praised Weinstein’s dedication, noting participants look forward to her Monday classes and appreciate the health and peace of mind she provides. Weinstein, originally from New York, moved to San Diego after college and now resides in Solana Beach with her dogs. She spent over 20 years in digital advertising before transitioning to yoga teaching after completing two 200-hour trainings. Her chair yoga sessions focus on community and well-being, offering a space for connection and relaxation. Weinstein emphasized that yoga is about feeling good in one’s body, not flexibility. She described her classes as opportunities to slow down, move, and leave feeling better. DMCC, a nonprofit supporting older adults, highlighted Weinstein’s role in promoting wellness and independence. Details about her class and volunteer opportunities are available on dmcc.cc/volunteerofthemonth.
